notes: lambda_even is the empirically distinguished smallest-positive eigenvalue of the finite-T even-sector Galerkin matrix at c=100, N=150, T=800, dps=500, flint_prec=2000; it is not the raw minimum and is not asserted as a theorem-level ground-state identification for this truncated cell. The same finite-T matrix has five negative-sign eigenvalues at log10|e| in {-40.66, -59.75, -96.75, -165.15, -223.69}. Their leading recorded values are stable in the dps=500-vs-1000 comparison but they disappear when the archimedean cutoff T is increased, so ERRATA.md identifies them as finite-T archimedean-cutoff artifacts. Continuum positivity is RH-equivalent and is not assumed here. The associated smallest-positive eigenvector is the branch used for the gamma extraction; no claim that it equals the raw finite-T minimum is intended.
